statement: Today Lea is 7 years old and her brother is 3. In how many years will their ages add up to 30?

choices.misconception: I found the brother's age at that time instead of the number of years.
I found Lea's age at that time instead of the number of years.
I thought their total grows by 1 each year, forgetting that both of them get older.
I subtracted only Lea's age from 30.

hints: How much does the total of their ages grow each year?
Each year both children get one year older, so their total age grows by 2 every year. Find how much the total still has to grow.
Today the total is 7 + 3 = 10, so it must grow by 20, at 2 per year.

solutions.reliable: Today their ages add up to 7 + 3 = 10. Every year both get one year older, so the total grows by 2 each year. It must grow by 30 - 10 = 20, which takes 20 ÷ 2 = 10 years. Check: in 10 years Lea is 17 and her brother 13, and 17 + 13 = 30. The transferable idea: in age problems everyone ages at the same rate, so a total of several ages grows by one year per person per year.

whyOnTest: Age problems test whether you remember that every person gets older, so a total of ages grows faster than one person's age.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
